chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a hadith: 'Indeed, in mutual hatred is the 'shaver' (that which shaves away). I do not mean the shaver of hair, but the shaver of the Religion.'

key_terms.التَّبَاغُضِ: Mutual hatred or enmity between people
key_terms.الْحَالِقَةَ: The shaver; that which cuts off or strips away completely
key_terms.حَالِقَةَ الدِّينِ: The shaver of the Religion (spiritual stripping of faith)

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean by the 'shaver of the Religion' in the context of hatred?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) uses the metaphor of 'shaving' (haliqa) to describe how mutual hatred erodes the core of faith, distinguishing it from the physical act of shaving hair. This concept is central to Shia ethics regarding silat al-rahim (severing ties), where internal animosity is viewed as more destructive than mere physical separation, effectively stripping the believer of their spiritual integrity. The narration underscores that hatred does not just break social bonds but actively dismantles the religious structure of the individual.
